visuals.label: Figure 2
visuals.caption: Framework of XPSR. (a) First, we integrate an MLLM to acquire semantic priors, encompassing both high-level and low-level descriptions for the LR image. Two varieties of embeddings are derived upon input into the CLIP text encoder. (b) Next, the LR image, along with the embeddings above, are input into the controlled diffu- sion model as conditions through a Semantic-Fusion Attention (SFA), adhering to the defined workflow. Besides, a Degradation-Free Constraint (DFC) is appended to the ControlNet part, alleviating the challenge of discerning distortions.

visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: The two text streams enter parallel branches in Semantic-Fusion Attention (SFA). The fused image-conditioned representation controls denoising through added Conditional Attention. High-level semantics also condition the U-Net, while low-level semantics are used in ControlNet rather than directly in the noisy U-Net branch. Clean image and clean latent targets supervise intermediate ControlNet representations only during training. There is no clean reference available at inference.

The palm example additionally discusses composition and focus of attention. Thus these prompts are rich but noisy semantic observations, not guaranteed ground truth about the camera or codec. A robust method must tolerate this mismatch rather than treat the sentences as exact measurements.

visuals.classification_reason: Required to evaluate this specific evidence: On DIV2K, MANIQA is 0.5046→0.6080, CLIPIQA 0.6959→0.7816, MUSIQ 68.35→69.99. Differences are +0.1034, +0.0857 and +1.64 score units; relative changes are approximately 20.49%, 12.32% and 2.40%. The paper’s “10.34%, 8.57%, 1.64%” wording is therefore not standard relative-change arithmetic. Meanwhile PSNR falls 23.56→22.80, LPIPS worsens 0.3283→0.3761 and FID 28.89→33.38. The supported conclusion is improved no-reference perceptual quality with a measurable reference-fidelity trade-off, not simultaneous superiority in all senses.
